data.long_meaning: Thalabah is an Arabic name for a gardener or one who tends to the land. It is derived from the Arabic word 'thalabah' which means 'to till the soil', 'to cultivate' or 'to plant'. This name is a beautiful reminder of the importance of nurturing and caring for the natural world around us.

data.cultural_impact: Thalabah is a name that is deeply rooted in Islamic culture, reflecting the rich agricultural heritage of the Islamic world. The name speaks to the tradition of working the land and cultivating the earth, which has been a part of Islamic societies for centuries. This connection to the land and agriculture is emphasized in the Quran, where Verses like "And it is He Who hath produced you from the earth and settles you in it: a shape were ye before quite naught: then He hath raised amongst you some of His serving-men, and made youClassNameIndividuals in a race one of another: and He is the true God, in Whose Hand are all things. (Surah Ar-Ra'd 13:3) and "And it is not for a soul to believe except with that which Allah hath opened (its heart)" (Surah Al Baqarah 2:28) Considered the person Thalabah to be one who is dedicating himself to cultivating not only the physical land but also nurturing the hearts and souls of people, making the name a powerful reminder of the importance of both sustainable agriculture and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Thalabah also holds profound spiritual significance in Islamic traditions. It speaks to the idea that we are all called to till the soil of our own spiritual lives, to cultivate our character and nurture our inner gardens. In the Quran, Allah says "And follow the best of the ways of men, most near to righteousness: such men are those who believe and follow all that is sent down by their Lord, and it is they who are saved" (Surah Al Qasas 28:85) This verse and many others emphasize the importance of following the best ways, which can be likened to being a good gardener: waters the seeds of good deeds covered by patience, weeds out the bad deeds, and nurtures the heart and soul with the fertile soil of knowledge, wisdom and prayers. The spiritual significance of the name Thalabah also highlights the importance of being present in the moment, working diligently on our personal growth and development, as the best gardener does not merely rely on the past or the future, but truly honors and cherishes the present.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt), 2nd/8th century CE The name Thalabah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Narrates an episode where Saladin's general, 'Imad ad-Din Zengi, marched to Aswan in Upper Egypt to deal with a rebellion. The rebel leader, Thalabah ibn Ruzzik, was a Christian Copt, was defeated and captured. Zengi had Thalabah's eyes gouged out and his hands cut off, as a warning to other rebels.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Wasil, Mudhakkirat Ibn Wasil (Memoirs of Ibn Wasil), 7th/13th century CE The name Thalabah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mentions Thalabah ibn Ruzzik as the governor of Aswan during the Ayyubid period. He was a notable figure who expanded the city's irrigation systems, fortifications, and facilitated trade.

Additionally, it is popular among individuals seeking spiritual growth and self-improvement, as a reminder to always be a student of life and the world around them.
